name: HP Inc.
description: HP sells laptops, desktops and workstations (about 70 percent of revenue) and printers plus the ink and toner they use (about 30 percent). The PC half earns thin margins of about 5 percent on boxes sold through retailers and to businesses. The printing half earns about 19 percent margins and nearly all of HP's operating profit because printers are sold cheaply to lock in years of high-margin supplies (ink and toner were $10.9B of FY2025 revenue and 65 percent of printing sales). Memory and storage cost inflation and tariffs are the main margin risks the company names.

businessLines.name: Personal Systems
businessLines.how: One-time hardware sale of each device to businesses, governments and consumers through retail, distributors and direct channels; revenue is units times average selling price, with small attached services and subscriptions.
businessLines.description: Desktops, notebooks, workstations (including AI PCs), thin clients, point-of-sale systems, displays, plus software, endpoint security and lifecycle services.

revenue.note: FY2024 $36,195M (+6.5 percent); Commercial PS $27,438M (+7.7 percent), Consumer PS $11,094M (+1.1 percent). Q3 FY2026 $11,767M vs $9,931M; nine months $32,231M vs $28,179M.

businessLines.name: Printing: Supplies
businessLines.how: Recurring replacement purchases of cartridges by owners of HP printers, plus subscription programs; high margin because the printer base is the installed customer base.
businessLines.description: Ink and laser cartridges, media, industrial graphics supplies and 3D printing supplies.

revenue.note: FY2024 $11,295M (-2.2 weighted points). Q3 FY2026 $2,536M vs $2,609M.

businessLines.name: Printing: Commercial and Consumer printer hardware
businessLines.how: One-time printer hardware sale (often at thin margin) plus managed print and device service contracts; the printer feeds the supplies stream above.
businessLines.description: Office printers and print solutions for SMBs, public sector and enterprises (Commercial); home printers (Consumer); plus graphics and 3D printing and personalization for industrial markets.

revenue.note: Commercial Printing $4,633M plus Consumer Printing $1,153M (computed); FY2024 $4,841M and $1,202M. Whole Printing segment $16,702M (-3.7 percent), operating profit $3,118M (18.7 percent margin).
